swap_submitted_at_1000.meaning: Alice's swap transaction (3000 USDC to 1 WETH, minimum 2990 USDC worth) was submitted at 10:00 AM
swap_submitted_at_1000.checkpoint: before execution, at submission time 10:00 AM

tx_pending_low_gas.meaning: the submitted transaction has low gas priority and remains pending in the mempool during network congestion
tx_pending_low_gas.checkpoint: before execution, while pending in mempool

market_crash_percent.meaning: market price change since submission, reported as -20 (a 20% crash) by 3:00 PM

stale_execution_occurred.meaning: the stale pending swap transaction executed hours after submission (at 3:00 PM) despite drastically changed market conditions, forcing acceptance of outdated slippage parameters

assumptions: The swap functions are callable without any additional authorization condition; the report asserts no unauthorized-caller precondition.
The 10:30 AM deadline value appears only in a hypothetical 'with deadline protection' scenario and is not an actual submitted parameter, so it is not encoded.
The transaction executing at 3:00 PM is presented as an example scenario rather than a confirmed on-chain event; the plan formalizes the report-supported conditional scenario.

unresolved.description: Report does not specify the exact slippage percentage bound; 'up to slippage % value loss' is left unquantified, so the magnitude of forced slippage acceptance cannot be numerically encoded.
Report does not state a concrete deadline timestamp as an actual submitted parameter; the deadline-based rejection relation is represented only through the qualitative stale-execution observable.

limitations: The safety relation is expressed as absence of stale execution under the reported pending/low-gas/market-crash scenario; the deadline comparison itself is not numerically bound because no actual deadline parameter is reported.
Only the forced_execution_stale_prices impact is formalized; the MEV-targeting impact is handled in a separate claim-generation pass.
